Read the poem aloud and then recite it to the class: Whose Child is This? “Whose child is this?” I asked one day Seeing a little one out at play. “Mine”, said the parent with a tender smile. “Mine to keep a little while To bathe his hands and comb his hair, To tell him what he is to wear, To prepare him that he may always be good. And each day do the things he should.” “Whose child is this?” I asked again, As the door opened and someone came in said the teacher with the same tender smile.
